directory and bare directory exclusions warn instead of being imported.
Yamlfmt matches paths relative to the invocation directory, with absolute patterns
matching only absolute inputs; migration assumes the config directory as the root.
Standard matching,
`regex_exclude`, and source `include` settings still warn.

Local dprint `extends` paths resolve relative to the extending file. Earlier bases
take precedence over later bases, and the extending config wins over its bases;
exclusions accumulate. Cycles, excessive inheritance, URLs, and unresolved paths
skip that source with a hint to flatten the configuration locally. Migration never
fetches shared configurations.

Imports report the same lint/format conflict notices as `ryl format`, using the
effective colocated lint configuration. Imported settings stay unchanged.

Unsupported settings produce warnings on stderr and comments in generated TOML.
Migration preserves YAML values and properties rather than adopting destructive
source behavior. Migration also keeps ryl's default
[YAML 1.1 reader compatibility](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/yaml-version/); a source formatter does not
establish which YAML readers consume your files. Config migration leaves source
ignore comments unchanged unless you opt into [comment conversion](#suppression-comments).

| Gap | Migration behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forced quoting of plain strings | Retains existing quote presentation; warns when forcing was requested |
| Other per-file overrides or shared configurations | Warns about unsupported overrides; follows local dprint inheritance, but never fetches remote configurations |
| Source-specific flow wrapping, bracket padding, or trailing commas | Uses supported ryl layout settings; warns about differences |
| yamlfmt YAML merge keys | Retains the source without importing formatter settings; expand merged settings manually and rerun |
| yamlfmt scalar spellings requiring unsupported resolution | Retains the source without importing formatter settings; quote string values, use plain decimal numbers, or configure ryl manually |
| Removing document-start markers | Removes the first optional marker; retains required boundaries |
| yamlfix null spelling and per-style prose behavior | Preserves null spellings and uses split-only line folding; warns |
| Dimensions outside ryl's supported range | Uses a supported fallback and warns |

## Suppression comments

Convert configs first, then comments; comment conversion also works with an existing
ryl config:

1. Preview comment changes with the first command below.
2. Apply with `--migrate-write` after reviewing the diff and warnings.
3. Run `ryl format --diff .` and, with lint rules enabled, `ryl check .`.

```bash
ryl --migrate-directives --migrate-from prettier --migrate-root .
ryl --migrate-directives --migrate-from prettier --migrate-root . --migrate-write

# Combine config import and comment conversion
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-directives --migrate-from yamlfmt --migrate-write
```

Without `--migrate-write`, source changes appear as unified diffs. `--migrate-root`
can select one application file or a directory; selecting a config file does not
implicitly scan its parent. Static source configuration is discovered independently
of existing ryl settings. Competing formatter configurations require `--migrate-from`;
use the same flag when no source config identifies the formatter.

| Source comment | Conversion |
| :--- | :--- |
| Active `# yamllint disable`, `enable`, `disable-line`, first-line `disable-file` | Equivalent `# ryl` spelling; rule selection and targets stay unchanged |
| `# prettier-ignore` | `# ryl format-ignore` when the comment protects the same YAML node |
| pretty_yaml's configured ignore marker | `# ryl format-ignore` when the comment protects the same YAML node |
| First-line `# !yamlfmt!:ignore` | `# ryl format-disable` for one document without an explicit end marker |

Only actual YAML comments change, including supported Markdown YAML regions. Scalar
contents and unrelated bytes remain unchanged. Formatter conversions preserve formatting
only; lint and safe lint fixes remain active. No additional runtime aliases are installed.

Retained comments are left in their original spelling with a warning. Review them
manually when migration cannot prove which YAML node or region a comment protects:

- Inline markers, reason suffixes, tags or anchors, explicit keys, flow members,
  document crossings, or existing ryl formatter directives.
- Markers shared with lint directives, or source per-file, plugin or pragma settings
  that change the protected region. A non-first-line `# !yamlfmt!:ignore` has no
  proven equivalent; choose a native node or region directive manually.
- Prettier Markdown outside supported front matter and lowercase `yaml` fences.
  Embedded formatting and a matching parser must be enabled; Quarto and R Markdown
  need an explicit data-only Markdown parser configuration.
- Dprint plugins other than official pretty_yaml `0.5.x` or `0.6.0` (official WASM
  URLs may include checksums), remote inheritance, or custom file associations.
- Shared comment segments outside the supported legacy directive grammar.

YAML-only Prettier overrides without parser, plugin, or pragma options permit YAML
comment conversion. Overrides provably limited to other literal extensions, such
as `*.md`, do not block YAML conversion. Other overrides retain source markers.
Every directive run reports converted and retained comment totals plus skipped
file counts; reruns still report unsupported retained markers.

Writes preserve supported encodings and BOMs. Files whose bytes cannot round-trip
through their encoding are retained. Previews report when encodings, line endings or
filenames prevent a text diff. Source configs are excluded from application writes;
symlinks stay unchanged. Combined migration cleans up eligible configs only after
application writes succeed.

## Source cleanup

| Source | `--migrate-delete-old` / `--migrate-rename-old` |
| :--- | :--- |
| yamllint, recognized standalone yamlfmt or yamlfix | Eligible after successful import with understood settings |
| Prettier, dprint, `package.json`, `package.yaml`, `pyproject.toml` | Always retained because they can configure other tools; remove obsolete YAML settings manually |

Custom filenames, sources with unknown settings, skipped sources, and inherited
sources outside the migration root remain untouched, with a warning.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamlfix/

# Migrating from yamlfix

Import the settings first (a successful import exits `0`; inspect warnings):

```bash
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from yamlfix --migrate-stdout
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from yamlfix --migrate-write
```

Follow [After migrating](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-formatters/#after-migrating) to verify
formatting and update CI, or use the manual profile below.

`ryl format` covers most of [yamlfix](https://github.com/lyz-code/yamlfix)'s
options through `[format]` keys and the top-level `line-length` and
`indent-width`. Replace `yamlfix .` with `ryl format .`, and `yamlfix --check .`
with `ryl format --check .`. The mapping and `--migrate-from yamlfix` import follow
yamlfix 1.19.1; older configurations may work, but defaults follow that release.

ryl reads configuration from `.ryl.toml`, `ryl.toml` or `[tool.ryl]` in
`pyproject.toml`, or the file passed with `-c`. It does not read `YAMLFIX_*`
environment variables.

ryl defaults to indent width 2. Set top-level `indent-width` explicitly to keep
another width.

## Manual configuration

A yamlfix configuration:

```toml
[tool.yamlfix]
line_length = 100
explicit_start = false
whitelines = 1
comments_min_spaces_from_content = 1
```

becomes:

```toml
[tool.ryl]
line-length = 100

[tool.ryl.format]
fold-long-lines = true
document-start = "remove"
max-blank-lines = 1
comment-spacing = 1
```

## Option mapping

| yamlfix option (default) | ryl equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `comments_min_spaces_from_content` (2) | `[format] comment-spacing` (default 2) |
| `comments_require_starting_space` (true) | `[format] comment-starting-space = "add"`; `false` maps to `"preserve"` |
| `whitelines` (0) | `[format] max-blank-lines` (default 2), see [blank lines](#blank-lines) |
| `comments_whitelines` (1) | none, see [blank lines](#blank-lines) |
| `section_whitelines` (0) | none, see [blank lines](#blank-lines) |
| `explicit_start` (true) | `[format] document-start = "add"`; `false` maps to `"remove"` |
| `indent_mapping` (2) | top-level `indent-width` |
| `indent_sequence` (4), `indent_offset` (2) | top-level `indent-width` with `[format] indent-sequences` selects indented or flush sequences; independent sequence width and offset have no exact equivalent |
| `line_length` (80) | top-level `line-length` with `[format] fold-long-lines = true` |
| `preserve_quotes` (false) | `true` maps to `[format] quote-style = "preserve"`; for `false`, `quote-style = "single"` or `"double"` is the closest match, see [forcing quotes](#forcing-quotes) |
| `quote_representation` (`'`) | `[lint.rules.quoted-strings] quote-type = "single"` or `"double"`, see [forcing quotes](#forcing-quotes) |
| `quote_basic_values`, `quote_keys_and_basic_values` (false) | see [forcing quotes](#forcing-quotes) |
| `none_representation` (`""`) | none: ryl keeps each null as written |
| `sequence_style` (`flow_style`) | `[format] sequence-style`; `[format] mapping-style` controls mappings. See [collection style](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#collection-style) for refusal cases |
| `allow_duplicate_keys` (false) | none: not a formatting concern; the `key-duplicates` lint rule reports them |
| `config_path` | none: ryl discovers its own config, or `-c` takes a translated config file |

## Differences in behaviour

### Blank lines

- yamlfix's `whitelines = N` sets every run of blank lines to exactly N, so it
  expands an existing run that is shorter. ryl's `max-blank-lines` only caps a
  run.
- ryl has no separate count before comment lines (`comments_whitelines`), and
  never adds blank lines around multi-line top-level entries
  (`section_whitelines`).

### Comment spacing

yamlfix only changes the gap before an inline comment when
`comments_min_spaces_from_content` is above 1. ryl's `comment-spacing` always
sets the gap exactly, so `comment-spacing = 1` also shrinks a wider gap.

### Removing `---`

yamlfix's `explicit_start = false` removes document start markers, which merges
the documents of a multi-document stream. Imported `document-start = "remove"`
removes only the first optional marker; directives, empty documents and stream
separators keep required markers.

### Forcing quotes

ryl's formatter quotes only where a value needs quotes. To quote every plain
string, as yamlfix's `quote_basic_values` does, enable the `quoted-strings`
lint rule with `required = true` and fix with `ryl check --fix`, and set
`[format] quote-style = "preserve"` so `ryl format` keeps the quotes. The
rule's `quote-type` picks the quote, as `quote_representation` does:

```toml
[format]
quote-style = "preserve"

[lint.rules.quoted-strings]
required = true
quote-type = "single"
```

`quote_representation` only applies when force-quoting. ryl's
`[format] quote-style` instead sets the quote for every string that needs one,
so it approximates yamlfix's quoting rather than matching it.

Add `check-keys = true` to quote keys too, as `quote_keys_and_basic_values`
does.

### Rewrites ryl does not do

- yamlfix rewrites `yes`, `on` and similar to `true`/`false`. Under YAML 1.2
  those are strings, so the rewrite changes values; ryl leaves them.
- yamlfix escapes Jinja `{{ }}` templates. ryl refuses YAML it cannot parse.
- yamlfix's `line_length` also joins lines the author broke. ryl only splits
  lines longer than `line-length`, and only when `fold-long-lines` is on.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamlfmt/

# Migrating from google/yamlfmt

Import the basic formatter settings first (a successful import exits `0`; inspect warnings):

```bash
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from yamlfmt --migrate-stdout
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from yamlfmt --migrate-write
```

Follow [After migrating](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-formatters/#after-migrating) to verify
formatting, convert comments and update CI, or use the manual profile below.

The [config importer](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-formatters/) imports `exclude` when
`match_type: doublestar`, anchoring patterns to the configuration directory.
The importer cleans relative path components and rebases absolute paths inside
that directory; paths outside the directory and bare directory exclusions warn.
Yamlfmt matches the paths produced by its include globs from the invocation
directory, so use the configuration directory as the migration root.
Standard matching, `regex_exclude`, and `include` settings still warn.

Replace `yamlfmt .` with `ryl format .` and `yamlfmt -lint .` with
`ryl format --check .`. The settings below approximate the default basic formatter
in google/yamlfmt 0.21.0. They were compared on the same YAML inputs with
`yamlfmt -in` and `ryl format -`.

ryl defaults to indent width 2. Set top-level `indent-width` explicitly to keep
another width.

## Manual configuration

```toml
# .ryl.toml
indent-width = 2

[format]
quote-style = "preserve"
comment-spacing = 1
max-blank-lines = 0
```

`quote-style = "preserve"` keeps existing quotes, as yamlfmt did in the comparison.
`comment-spacing = 1` matches its inline comments. Its basic formatter removes
blank lines between entries; `max-blank-lines = 0` does the same. Both indent
sequences under mapping keys by two spaces and use LF in the tested environment.
See the [formatter settings](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#configuration) for other options.

## Option mapping

`formatter.*` below names keys nested under `formatter:`, rather than top-level keys:

```yaml
formatter:
  indent: 4
```

| yamlfmt setting | ryl equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `formatter.indent: 2` | top-level `indent-width = 2` |
| `formatter.pad_line_comments: 1` | `[format] comment-spacing = 1` |
| `formatter.line_ending: lf` | `[format] line-ending = "lf"` (default) |
| `formatter.line_ending: crlf` | `[format] line-ending = "cr-lf"` |
| `formatter.include_document_start: false` (default) | `[format] document-start = "remove"`; see [markers](#document-markers) |
| `formatter.include_document_start: true` | `[format] document-start = "add"` |
| `formatter.max_line_length: 0` | `[format] fold-long-lines = false` (default) |
| `formatter.max_line_length: 40` | Approximately: top-level `line-length = 40` and `[format] fold-long-lines = true` |

At 40 columns, yamlfmt wraps plain scalars differently and wraps flow sequences that ryl leaves on one line unless `sequence-expand` is set.

## Deliberate differences

### Document markers

yamlfmt removes `---` and `...` from a single document in the tested default
profile. Imported `document-start = "remove"` removes the first optional `---`;
directives, empty documents and separators keep required markers. Existing `...`
markers remain. `document-start = "add"` adds missing `---` if required.

### Layout and values

yamlfmt reprints the document, including removing blank lines. ryl edits the
existing text and keeps any construct that cannot be safely restyled. In the
comparison, yamlfmt kept existing flow collections and quote styles; ryl's
`sequence-style = "preserve"` and `mapping-style = "preserve"` do likewise.
For inputs involving tags, aliases, or unusual scalars, run `ryl format --diff .`
before replacing the formatter: ryl retains the parsed values, comments, and
anchors rather than matching yamlfmt's reprint at any cost.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-prettier/

# Migrating from Prettier

Import the YAML settings first (a successful import exits `0`; inspect warnings):

```bash
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from prettier --migrate-stdout
ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-from prettier --migrate-write
```

Follow [After migrating](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-formatters/#after-migrating) to verify
formatting, convert comments and update CI, or use the manual profile below.

For YAML files, run `ryl format .` to write changes and
`ryl format --check .` in CI. Keep Prettier for other file types. The settings below follow
Prettier 3.9.10's YAML output on the same inputs used with `ryl format -`.
Prettier's [general options](https://prettier.io/docs/options) can alter the
starting profile.

The [config importer](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-formatters/) applies supported YAML-only
overrides in source order and imports `.prettierignore`, including negations.
Unsupported override scopes still warn; inspect the generated configuration before
replacing Prettier.

ryl defaults to indent width 2. Set top-level `indent-width` explicitly to keep
another width.

## Manual configuration

```toml
# .ryl.toml
indent-width = 2

[format]
quote-style = "double"
brace-spacing = true
comment-spacing = 1
max-blank-lines = 1
sequence-expand = "auto"
mapping-expand = "auto"
property-order = "tag-first"
```

`brace-spacing = true` produces `{ a: 1 }` while leaving `{}` tight.
`comment-spacing = 1` matches inline comments; `max-blank-lines = 1` matches
the tested collapse of a longer blank run. Both tools indent nested sequences
by two spaces and write LF in the tested profile.

## Option mapping

| Prettier option (default) | ryl equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `tabWidth: 2` | top-level `indent-width = 2` |
| `singleQuote: false` | `[format] quote-style = "double"`; see [quotes](#quotes) |
| `bracketSpacing: true` | `[format] brace-spacing = true` |
| `endOfLine: "lf"` | `[format] line-ending = "lf"` (default) |
| `printWidth: 80` | top-level `line-length = 80` plus `[format] fold-long-lines = true` is only an approximation; see [long lines](#long-lines) |

## Deliberate differences

### Quotes

Prettier keeps the quotes around `"hello"`; ryl removes them when the scalar
can be plain, even with `quote-style = "double"`. The setting chooses double
quotes only for strings that still need quoting. Use `quote-style = "preserve"`
if retaining existing quotes matters more than normalizing their style.

### Long lines

Prettier expands a long flow sequence into multiple lines at its print width.
ryl preserves the flow sequence by default; `sequence-expand = "auto"` and
`mapping-expand = "auto"` write Prettier's layout instead, including its move of a
value that fits alone on the line after its key and its `key: [` form for a collection
followed by a comment. Two things differ. ryl keeps that comment on the `[` line, where
Prettier puts it after the `]`, so the comment stays beside the data it followed. And the
columns follow ryl's `indentation` rule: in a sequence entry (`- [`) and before a trailing
comment, entries sit two past the start of the line rather than past the `[` or the key,
and the `]` one past it.
`fold-long-lines = true` folds eligible scalar text at `line-length`, and may fold
scalars that Prettier keeps on one line.

### Layout and markers

Prettier reprints the document. ryl retains existing `---` and `...` markers,
flow or block collection style, comments, and anchors unless a safe formatting
pass changes them. Prettier also retains markers in the tested input, but the
two formatters may choose different whitespace around the same YAML value.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/

# ryl Rules Reference

## A comprehensive reference of all YAML linting rules

## Introduction

ryl implements 30 rules for checking YAML files. This page is a categorised
index of every rule with a brief description and a link to its detailed
documentation. Each rule page covers what the rule does, why it matters,
configuration options, and (where applicable) automatic fix behaviour.

For configuration discovery, presets, and file selection, see
[Configuration presets](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/config-presets/).

## Rule categories

- [Layout and spacing](#layout-and-spacing) &mdash; whitespace, indentation,
  line endings, line length
- [Document structure](#document-structure) &mdash; document markers, empty
  values, anchors, tags, keys
- [Comments](#comments) &mdash; comment placement and spacing
- [Values](#values) &mdash; numeric, string, and boolean value formats

Rules that auto-fix are marked with :wrench: in the **Fix** column, and rules with an
[unsafe fix](#unsafe-fixes) with :warning:. Most layout
rules are also enforced by [`ryl format`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/); the
[Formatter](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules) page lists which, and the options that
conflict with it.

## Layout and spacing

| Rule | Description | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| [`block-scalar-chomping`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/block-scalar-chomping/) | Explicit chomping indicator (`-`/`+`) on block scalars. |  |
| [`braces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/) | Spaces inside flow mapping braces (`{...}`). | :wrench: |
| [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/) | Spaces inside flow sequence brackets (`[...]`). | :wrench: |
| [`colons`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/colons/) | Spaces around mapping colons. | :wrench: |
| [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) | Spaces around flow collection commas. | :wrench: |
| [`empty-lines`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-lines/) | Number of consecutive empty lines. | :wrench: |
| [`hyphens`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/hyphens/) | Spaces after sequence hyphens. | :wrench: |
| [`indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/) | Block indentation, sequence indentation, multi-line strings. |  |
| [`line-length`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/line-length/) | Maximum line length. |  |
| [`new-line-at-end-of-file`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-line-at-end-of-file/) | A trailing newline at end of file. | :wrench: |
| [`new-lines`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-lines/) | Consistent line endings (LF vs CRLF). | :wrench: |
| [`trailing-spaces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/trailing-spaces/) | Trailing whitespace at end of lines. | :wrench: |
| [`unicode-line-breaks`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/unicode-line-breaks/) | Raw NEL / LS / PS characters (not YAML 1.2 line breaks). |  |

## Document structure

| Rule | Description | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| [`anchors`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/anchors/) | Anchor and alias declarations and usage. |  |
| [`document-end`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-end/) | Document end marker `...`. | :wrench: |
| [`document-start`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-start/) | Document start marker `---`. | :wrench: |
| [`empty-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-values/) | Empty values in mappings and sequences. |  |
| [`key-duplicates`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-duplicates/) | Duplicate keys in mappings. |  |
| [`key-ordering`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-ordering/) | Alphabetical or configured ordering of mapping keys. | :wrench: |
| [`merge-keys`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/merge-keys/) | The `<<` merge key (a YAML 1.1 feature removed in 1.2). |  |
| [`tags`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/tags/) | Unsafe and non-portable YAML tags. |  |
| [`schema`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/schema/) | Validate against user-supplied local JSON Schemas. |  |
| [`yaml-directive`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/yaml-directive/) | A `%YAML` version directive on every document. | :wrench: |

## Comments

| Rule | Description | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| [`comments`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments/) | Spaces after `#` and before inline comments. | :wrench: |
| [`comments-indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments-indentation/) | Comment alignment with surrounding content. | :wrench: |

## Values

| Rule | Description | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| [`float-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/float-values/) | Float value formats. |  |
| [`octal-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/octal-values/) | Octal value formats. | :warning: |
| [`quoted-strings`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/quoted-strings/) | Quoted string styles and when to require quotes. | :wrench: |
| [`schema-dependent-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/schema-dependent-values/) | Plain values YAML 1.1 and 1.2 read differently (`2026-10-10`, `22:22`, `1_000`). | :warning: |
| [`truthy`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/truthy/) | Truthy values like `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`. | :wrench: :warning: |

## Severity levels

Warnings return exit code `0` unless strict mode is enabled with `--strict` or
TOML [`[lint] strict = true`](getting-started/quickstart.md#strict-mode).
Use `--no-strict` to override a configured strict mode for one run.

Every rule can be configured to report at either `error` (the default for
most rules) or `warning`. Errors cause `ryl` to exit non-zero; warnings are
printed and fail the run only under strict mode.

Configure the severity inline with the rule:

```toml
[lint.rules.line-length]
level = "warning"
max = 120
```

## Enabling and disabling rules

Toggle a rule on or off with a top-level string in the `[lint.rules]` table:

```toml
[lint.rules]
truthy = "disable"
key-ordering = "enable"
```

Enabling a rule without options applies its defaults. To enable every rule,
including the ryl-only ones, use `ALL`:

```toml
[lint.rules]
ALL = "enable"
truthy = "disable"

[lint.rules.line-length]
max = 120
```

Each rule then runs with its own defaults at level `error`. An explicit entry for
a rule wins over `ALL` wherever it appears in the table. `ALL` is TOML-only;
yamllint-compatible YAML config rejects it.

!!! warning "`ALL` can grow when you upgrade ryl"

    `ALL`, in config or as `--enable ALL`, turns on every rule the installed ryl
    has, including any added after you wrote the config. An upgrade that adds a rule
    can then fail a check that passed before. Pin the ryl version, or list the rules
    you want.

`ryl check --enable <RULES>` picks the rules from the command line instead:
comma-separated rule IDs or `ALL`, and the flag can be repeated. It replaces the
config's selection, so only the listed rules run. A listed rule keeps the options
and level the config gives it, and runs at its defaults if the config disables
it or does not mention it. `--disable <RULES>` then subtracts comma-separated rule IDs
or `ALL` from the selection; pass `--disable` once per command. `ignore`,
`per-file-ignores` and inline directives
still apply. The flag works without any config file:

```bash
ryl check --enable ALL .
ryl check --enable truthy,line-length .
```

The built-in `default`
and `relaxed` presets cover the common starting points (the `empty` preset is
YAML-`extends:` only, with no usable TOML form); see
[Configuration presets](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/config-presets/).

To switch rules off for part of a file with `# ryl disable` /
`# yamllint disable` comments, see [Inline directives](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/directives/).

## Automatic fixing

The `--fix` flag applies safe fixes for rules marked with :wrench: above:

```bash
ryl check --fix .
```

Control which rules apply fixes with `fixable`/`unfixable` in the `[lint]` table:

```toml
[lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = ["comments"]
```

### Unsafe fixes

A safe fix never changes what a value means. An **unsafe** fix may: it picks one
meaning where readers disagree, so it applies only when you opt in, as with ruff.
`truthy`, `octal-values` and `schema-dependent-values` offer one for a plain scalar
that YAML 1.1 and 1.2 readers load differently (see
[YAML version compatibility](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/yaml-version/#unsafe-fixes-and-source-version)).

!!! warning "Check the source version first"

    Unsafe fixes default to YAML 1.2 meanings for undeclared files. For files
    written for PyYAML, Ansible or another YAML 1.1 reader, set
    `source-version = "1.1"` before applying them. Follow the
    [migration recipe](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/yaml-version/#migrate-undeclared-yaml-11-files-safely).

`ryl check` counts the fixes it left out:

```console
$ cat config.yaml
enabled: yes
$ ryl check config.yaml
config.yaml
  1:10      error    truthy value should be one of [false, true]  (truthy)

1 unsafe fix available with `--fix --unsafe-fixes`.
```

| Control | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--unsafe-fixes` or top-level `unsafe-fixes = true` | Permit unsafe fixes with `--fix`; preview with `--diff --unsafe-fixes` |
| `[lint] extend-safe-fixes = ["octal-values"]` | Let plain `--fix` apply that rule's unsafe fixes; use sparingly |
| `--no-unsafe-fixes` | Override the configured unsafe-fix setting |
| Top-level `unsafe-fixes = false` | Disable unsafe fixes and silence the count |
| `[lint] unfixable = ["truthy"]` | Block the rule's safe and unsafe fixes |

Once enabled, an unsafe fix's message names the old and new spelling
(`; unsafe fix: yes -> "yes"`). `ryl format` never applies unsafe fixes.
In an editor, `ryl server` offers each
rule's unsafe fixes as a quick fix, kept out of "Fix all" until the config applies
them.

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/schema/

# schema

In `ryl server`, clients supporting dynamic file watching register exact local schema
root and `$ref` paths, including missing files and arbitrary extensions. Creating,
saving or deleting a dependency revalidates open documents and updates push diagnostics
or requests a pull refresh. Local-only configurations require no network worker.
Unsaved schema buffers are not read; clients without dynamic registration must restart
the server or reopen documents after schema edits.

Hovering a key or value shows the prepared schema's `title` and `description`, even
when the value is invalid. Keys use their value's schema. Schema text is escaped plain
text, limited to 4,096 characters per annotation. Hover follows explicit `properties`,
homogeneous `items` and static `$ref` paths, with a 128-step limit; branches, tuple items,
dynamic references and documents containing aliases or merge keys receive no schema
hover. Direct properties beside unrelated branches remain available. A refused document
does not suppress hover in later documents unless the shared projection budget is exhausted.
References honor the resolved resource's dialect, including embedded resources reached
by JSON Pointer; Draft 7 and earlier ignore annotations beside `$ref`.
Hover never reads schema files, fetches resources or starts preparation. Pending or
unapproved schemas retain diagnostic explanations only. Files without associations
require no schema projection. Markdown regions use the host file's association.

## What this rule does

Validates YAML documents against user-supplied JSON Schemas. Schemas are supplied by the
project; ryl supplies no application-specific schema catalog. No fix is available.

## Configuration

TOML only, in `.ryl.toml`, `ryl.toml`, or `[tool.ryl.lint.rules.schema]` in
`pyproject.toml`. YAML configuration rejects `schema`.

<!-- ryl-config-check: skip -->
```toml
[lint.rules.schema]
level = "error"

[[lint.rules.schema.schemas]]
path = "schemas/github-workflow.json"
files = [".github/workflows/*.yml", ".github/workflows/*.yaml"]
```

| Setting | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `path` | Relative schema path, anchored at the config base directory. A config under `.config/` uses the parent directory. Exactly one of `path` or `url` is required. |
| `url` | HTTPS schema URL on port 443. The user must independently grant the origin. |
| `pins` | Optional map of full resource URLs to `sha256:<64 hex>` content pins. |
| `directives` | Default `false`. Enable per-document schema comment selection; the rule must also be enabled. |
| `files` | Optional path globs with `!` exclusions, like `key-ordering.orders`. Empty or omitted matches every file. |
| Association order | The first matching entry wins. Unmatched files and an enabled rule without associations are no-ops. |

`--stdin-filename` supplies the matching path for stdin. Anonymous stdin matches
only associations with empty `files`. Markdown regions match the host filename.
Normal rule directives, per-file ignores and per-line ignores apply.

## In-file directives

Opt in through TOML; comments never enable rules or grant network access:

```toml
[lint.rules.schema]
directives = true
```

Each YAML document can override its configured association with either header form:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=schemas/app.json
name: example
```

The short form is `# $schema: schemas/app.json`. Matching follows Red Hat's
yaml-language-server: prefixes are case-sensitive, whitespace after `#` is required,
and values end at whitespace. Quotes, percent signs and environment variables are
literal; paths containing spaces cannot be expressed. The first recognized modeline
wins, even when malformed: a missing value falls back to the configured association,
whereas an unloadable value is an error. `none`, case-insensitively, skips validation
for that document; `./none` names a file. Inline YAML `$schema` keys remain ordinary data.

Only header comments count, including comments around or on an opening `---`.
Root tags and anchors keep the header open until node content starts.
Leading `...` markers discard preceding headers without creating documents.
Comments after document content belong to that document; comments after `...` can
start the next header. Strings and block scalar bodies never select schemas.
Each enabled Markdown region has its own headers and uses the host filename.

Relative paths resolve beside the YAML or Markdown file but must remain inside the
canonical config root, including through symlinks. Absolute, drive, UNC and root `file:`
locations are refused. Anonymous stdin and untitled buffers need a filename for local
paths (`--stdin-filename` on the CLI); granted HTTPS URLs and `none` work without one.
Root fragments select JSON Pointers or anchors. HTTPS directives use the same grants,
pins, offline mode and retrieval limits as configured schemas.

Configured schemas still prepare eagerly, including overridden associations; a comment
cannot hide a broken configuration. Directive loading happens before lint-cache lookup.
Configured and directive resources share one preparation budget across documents and
Markdown regions. With directives off, comments incur no discovery scan or loading.

With directives enabled, key-ordering declines sorts that would move modelines,
including body comments that could become headers, and reports an unfixed notice.
Comment-spacing fixes preserve active and near-modeline
spellings. Formatting keeps these text protections without loading schemas.

## Loading and limits

Schemas compile during config resolution. Missing files, invalid schemas, unsupported
regex patterns, denied remote references and confinement failures are config errors (exit 2).
Both the root schema and referenced files must stay within the config base directory,
including after resolving symlinks. Absolute root paths and UNC references are refused.
Local roots retain confined `file:` references. Remote roots cannot read files.
Schema paths may contain spaces, brackets and other filename characters; `$ref`
URIs must percent-encode characters outside the URI path syntax.

Schema contents and local references contribute to the lint cache key. Schemas and
references share a 16 MiB byte limit and a 1,024-resource limit per config, bounding
what a large or hostile schema can cost. The limits are fixed.
Distinct URI aliases count separately toward both limits. Regex matching
uses a 100,000-step backtracking limit and 1 MiB compiled-pattern and DFA-cache limits. The draft
comes from `$schema`, defaulting to 2020-12.

## Remote schemas

Remote associations require a default-on `schema-network` build. A project requests
resources; grants come only from the launcher or user allowlist, including offline.
Every retrieved reference needs a grant for the resolved origin, even after `$id` rebasing.
`ryl server` prepares remote schemas in the background. Before accessing an ungranted
origin, the server reports an approval diagnostic on the affected file and configuration.
Use **Always allow `<origin>`** or **Allow once `<origin>`** from the diagnostic's quick
fixes. Allow once lasts for the server session; Always allow atomically updates the user
allowlist, refusing symlinks and non-regular files. A failed save reports a configuration
error and still grants access for the session. Workspace settings and project
configuration cannot grant access.

`server --offline` and `RYL_OFFLINE=1` disable approval actions and all DNS/HTTP access;
granted origins can still use cached schemas. Formatting never retrieves schemas.

<!-- ryl-config-check: skip -->
```toml
[[lint.rules.schema.schemas]]
url = "https://schemas.example.org/app.json"
files = ["app.yaml"]

[lint.rules.schema.pins]
"https://schemas.example.org/app.json" = "sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
```

```console
ryl check --schema-allow-origin https://schemas.example.org app.yaml
```

| User control | Behaviour |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--schema-allow-origin ORIGIN` | Repeatable exact HTTPS origin; no wildcard, path, query or fragment. |
| `RYL_SCHEMA_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Comma-separated origins, unioned with CLI grants. |
| User allowlist | `<user-config-dir>/ryl/allowed-schema-origins`, one origin per line, unioned with grants. |
| `--offline` / `RYL_OFFLINE=1` | No DNS or HTTP; cached full reference closure required. Stale entries are allowed. |
| `--no-cache` / `RYL_NO_CACHE=1` | Disable both lint and schema caches. Offline then cannot retrieve remote schemas. |
| `RYL_SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR` | Override the user schema cache (`<user-cache-dir>/ryl/schemas/v1`). |
| `--no-progress` | Suppress schema download messages on stderr. |

Only public destinations are accepted. Redirects, proxies, userinfo, encoded response
bodies and private/reserved IP addresses are refused. DNS checks the complete answer
before connecting, including mixed public/private answers. TLS uses bundled webpki roots.
Requests have a 5-second connect limit and a 30-second total limit; each process gets
64 requests and 60 seconds of network time. Query values are redacted in output.

Schema cache keys hash the complete canonical URL. Unpinned entries are fresh for
24 hours; stale entries refresh unconditionally. Pins are checked on every read and
permit indefinite reuse. Offline and pinned reads preserve fetch timestamps. Corrupt
entries are misses; symlinks are refused. Writes evict oldest entries above 256 MiB.

At load time, schemas with expanded weight above 1,000,000 are refused as
`schema too complex` (exit 2). The weight counts subschemas, declarations and
resolved references. Recursion without instance descent or with overlapping recursive
branches is also refused; distinct literal properties and disjoint object/array
paths are accepted. Repeated recursive tuple items are conservatively refused.
Drafts 04, 06 and 07 ignore keywords beside `$ref` during validation and complexity
screening. Unreferenced definitions are conservatively screened in newer drafts.
Draft 2019-09 `$recursiveRef` follows the validator's resource-root lookup even
when the reference contains a fragment. Dynamic references include all matching anchors as possible targets; this conservative
screen can refuse schemas whose runtime scopes would select fewer targets. Only
applicators and references active in the schema draft contribute to the screen.
More than 1,000,000 possible dynamic-reference edges are refused before expansion.

Projection is bounded to 1,000,000 nodes, 16 MiB of scalar and pointer storage, and
128 levels. A file reports at most 100 validation diagnostics plus a truncation note.
Users with no schema associations and directives disabled do no schema loading or projection. `ryl format`
does not load lint schemas.

## YAML values and locations

- Plain scalars resolve under YAML 1.2 core; explicit `%YAML 1.1` uses the existing
  version-aware resolver. Unsupported 1.1 values, including timestamps, are refused.
- Explicit YAML 1.1 float tags parse decimal or sexagesimal values rather than
  implicitly resolving integers (`!!float 012` is 12.0; `!!int 012` is 10).
- Explicit core tags must match the scalar's type and spelling; invalid tagged
  values produce `cannot validate` findings. The non-specific `!` tag resolves
  sequences and mappings as ordinary collections.
- Integers in the combined i64/u64 range and finite floats are supported.
- Aliases expand within the projection budget. Findings blame the alias use site.
- Merge keys, including aliased merge keys, expand before validation; explicit keys override inherited keys, and
  earlier mappings in merge sequences win. Malformed merges are refused.
- Duplicate decoded keys, non-string or complex keys and custom tags produce
  `cannot validate` findings (exit 1), rather than misleading type errors.
- Every document in a stream is validated independently; an empty document is null.
- Unexpected properties and invalid property names blame the key. Missing properties
  blame the containing mapping's start. Additional and unevaluated items blame the
  first offending item. Other findings use the instance value's source location.
- `oneOf` and `anyOf` findings select the most relevant branch error using
  [Python jsonschema's `best_match` heuristic](https://github.com/python-jsonschema/jsonschema/blob/main/jsonschema/exceptions.py).
  Equally ranked branches retain the summary. Messages mask instance values.

Editor diagnostics use the same engine. Watched schema-file edits invalidate prepared
schemas and revalidate affected documents. Schema completion is separate work.

Sources: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/specification),
[YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/).

---

Source: https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/

# Formatter

`ryl format` rewrites YAML files in place to a consistent layout. The formatter edits
only the spans that are off-style rather than reprinting the document, so the first run
on an existing project produces a small diff, and every later run on formatted files
changes nothing.

Biome does not format YAML, so there is no Biome YAML style to migrate.

## `ryl format`

```bash
# Format every YAML file under the current directory, in place
ryl format .

# Write nothing; exit 1 if any file would change, showing the change
ryl format --check .

# Write nothing; print a unified diff of the changes
ryl format --diff path/to/file.yaml

# Read stdin, write the formatted text to stdout
cat file.yaml | ryl format - --stdin-filename file.yaml
```

Inputs, file discovery, `.gitignore` handling and config discovery are the same as
`ryl check`. Unlike `ryl check`, `ryl format` needs no config: with none it formats
with the defaults below.

`--check` reports each file `ryl format` would change as one `unformatted` finding at
its first change, as ruff does. The `standard` and `colored` formats show the diff under
the finding. It uses the same reporters as `ryl check`, so it honours `--output-format`
and [`[output]`](output-formats.md) and picks the GitHub format in GitHub Actions.
`--check` and `--diff` end with a summary on stderr, such as
`1 file would be reformatted, 2 files already formatted`.

Already formatted files are skipped on later runs through the
[content-hash cache](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/quickstart/#caching). `--check` can also
reuse a clean result; `--diff` always generates the requested diff.

## Guarantees

Every edit `ryl format` makes is checked by property tests to be:

- **Value-preserving.** The document loads to the same data, with the same tags,
  anchors, aliases, key order and duplicate keys, resolved under the document's YAML
  version.
- **Comment-safe.** Every comment stays beside the node it annotates.
  With [schema directives](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/schema/#in-file-directives) enabled, comment spacing
  also preserves active and near-modeline spellings. Schema loading never runs during formatting.
- **Idempotent.** Formatting formatted output changes nothing.

### Syntax repairs and file handling

Root strings such as `'---'` and `'...'` retain their quotes because
the plain spellings are document markers. Marker prefixes followed by Unicode
whitespace also keep quotes for
[reference-parser compatibility](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/#marker-like-root-strings-and-unicode-whitespace).

Input rejected by strict YAML parsing is left alone and reported on stderr as
`skipped by ryl format`, with one exception: spec-invalid indentation, or a flow `?` key
with no space before the next indicator (`[?,]`), accepted by the parser's relaxed mode
can be repaired when the repaired text parses strictly and preserves the relaxed input's
values, tags, anchors and structure. `[?,]` becomes `[? ]`. Repairs print
`input was YAML the spec rejects; repaired it`; `--check` exits 1.
An unsafe or disabled repair leaves the entire file unchanged with a syntax skip.

`ryl check` and LSP diagnostics parse strictly and report the original indentation
as a syntax error. `check --fix`/`--diff`, LSP formatting and Fix All allow the same
guarded repair; lint fixes otherwise keep their existing rule selection.
Syntax repair in `check --fix`/`--diff` requires the default
`lint.fixable = ["ALL"]`, honors indentation ignore settings and uses formatter
indentation targets. Per-rule editor fixes leave syntax repair to Format Document
or Fix All.

See [File encodings](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/quickstart/#file-encodings) for encoding
preservation and `--check`/`--diff` behavior when a text patch cannot be emitted.
A document-prefix BOM stays before an added `---` marker, including in later
documents; the BOM does not count toward indentation. Diagnostic columns still
count a document-prefix BOM that remains in the source text.
The same exit behavior applies when a patch is skipped because the YAML ends in a
bare carriage return or the filename cannot be represented in a diff header.

### Jinja templates

ryl neither formats nor lints a Jinja template, since the rendered values can break
quotes ryl chose. A template is a file whose first line is a Salt renderer header that
runs Jinja, such as `#!jinja|yaml` or `#!yaml_jinja`. A directory scan skips one
silently, as it skips a `.j2` file; naming one, or piping one to stdin, exits `2`. A
file without the header is YAML, `{{ }}` included.

## Configuration

`ryl format` reads the `[format]` table of the same `.ryl.toml`, `ryl.toml` or
`pyproject.toml` (`[tool.ryl.format]`) that `ryl check` uses. A YAML
config cannot set it, so YAML-configured projects get the defaults.

```toml
[format]
quote-style = "single"
keep-quotes = false
line-ending = "lf"
document-start = "preserve"
document-end = "preserve"
prose-wrap = "preserve"
brace-spacing = false
comment-spacing = 2
comment-starting-space = "add"
max-blank-lines = 2
preview = false
sequence-style = "preserve"
mapping-style = "preserve"
sequence-expand = "preserve"
mapping-expand = "preserve"
property-order = "preserve"
indent-sequences = true
dash-on-own-line = false
```

### Choose settings by goal

Set the keys below inside `[format]`; `line-length` stays at the top level.
Here `*-style` and `*-expand` mean the corresponding `sequence-` and `mapping-` keys.

| Goal | Settings | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Block collections | `sequence-style = "block"`, `mapping-style = "block"` | Convert eligible flow collections to block |
| Short flow, long block | `sequence-style = "flow"`, `mapping-style = "flow"` | Choose style by `line-length` |
| One entry per line in existing flow | `sequence-expand = "always"`, `mapping-expand = "always"` | Keep block collections block |
| Wrap existing flow to fit | `sequence-expand = "auto"`, `mapping-expand = "auto"` | Try in place, below the key, then spread |
| Wrap prose and retain quotes | `prose-wrap = "always"`, `keep-quotes = true` | Join and wrap paragraphs without dropping optional quotes |

No single setting converts block collections to flow with one entry per line:
`*-style = "flow"` combined with `*-expand = "always"` leaves block collections block.

### Option reference

| Key | Default | Values | What it sets |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `quote-style` | `"single"` | `"single"`, `"double"`, `"preserve"` | The quote used where a string needs quoting; `"preserve"` leaves all quoting alone. See [Quote style](#quote-style). |
| `keep-quotes` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Keep existing optional quotes while `quote-style` selects their character. |
| `line-ending` | `"lf"` | `"lf"`, `"cr-lf"`, `"native"`, `"auto"` | Line endings, including the final newline; `"native"` is the platform's, and `"auto"` keeps the ending most of the file's lines use (`"lf"` on a tie or a file without line breaks). |
| `document-start` | `"preserve"` | `"add"`, `"preserve"`, `"remove"` | Add missing `---` markers, preserve markers, or remove the first optional marker. |
| `document-end` | `"preserve"` | `"add"`, `"preserve"` | Whether to add a missing `...` document end marker. |
| `prose-wrap` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | Preferred for new configs: preserve breaks, join and wrap paragraphs, or join without wrapping. See [Long lines](#long-lines). |
| `prose` | `[]` | Array of tables | Scoped token boundaries and protected regex spans, active only with `prose-wrap = "always"`. See [Expression wrapping](#expression-wrapping). |
| `fold-long-lines` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Legacy split-only folding at single spaces; cannot be combined with `prose-wrap`, even when false. |
| `brace-spacing` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Whether to write one space inside non-empty flow mapping braces, `{ a: 1 }`. Empty braces and brackets stay unpadded. |
| `comment-spacing` | `2` | `1` to `255` | Exact number of spaces between content and an inline comment. |
| `comment-starting-space` | `"add"` | `"add"`, `"preserve"` | Whether to add a missing space after a comment's `#`. |
| `max-blank-lines` | `2` | `0` to `255` | Most blank lines kept in a row between content lines; leading and trailing runs are removed. Scalar content is preserved, including keep-chomping (`\|+`/`>+`) tails; clip/strip tails can be trimmed. |
| `indent-sequences` | `true` | `true`, `false` | Whether a block sequence under a mapping key is indented past the key; `false` keeps it flush. |
| `dash-on-own-line` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Whether a block mapping in a block sequence starts on the line after its `-`; `false` joins them as `- name: web`. |
| `preview` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Opt in to style changes before they become stable. See [Preview style](#preview-style). |
| `sequence-style` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"block"`, `"flow"` | Collection style for sequences. See [Collection style](#collection-style). |
| `mapping-style` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"block"`, `"flow"` | Collection style for mappings. See [Collection style](#collection-style). |
| `sequence-expand` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"auto"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | Line breaks inside flow sequences. See [Flow line breaks](#flow-line-breaks). |
| `mapping-expand` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"auto"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | Line breaks inside flow mappings. See [Flow line breaks](#flow-line-breaks). |
| `property-order` | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"anchor-first"`, `"tag-first"` | The order of a node's anchor and tag on one line: `&a !!seq` or `!!seq &a`. |

Comment spacing targets leave ytt `#@` directives unchanged, including the gap
between an inline directive and its YAML content.

The top-level `line-length` and `indent-width` keys are shared with `ryl check`, where
they set the defaults for the `line-length` and `indentation` rules (see
[Quick start](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/quickstart/#configure-for-your-project)). `ryl format`
re-indents every block level to `indent-width`, and uses both as the fold width and
continuation indent under `fold-long-lines`.

Without `indent-width`, `ryl format` targets width 2. Set the top-level
`indent-width` to keep another width. Linting still defaults to
`spaces = "consistent"` when `indent-width` is unset.
If re-indenting would leave inconsistent indentation, `ryl format` keeps that
document's indentation and reports the sites it cannot fix.

The rest of the layout is fixed:

| Concern | `ryl format` writes |
| :--- | :--- |
| Own-line comments | Aligned with the content they precede |
| Flow collections | No spaces inside `[]` or empty `{}`, and inside other `{}` per `brace-spacing`; no space before a comma, one after; no trailing comma (`[a, b,]` becomes `[a, b]`) |
| Blank lines | None at the start or end of the file |
| Line ends | Remove trailing whitespace outside scalar content; add a final newline |
| After `-`, `?` and `:` | One space, re-indenting a compact collection that hangs on it |

Block scalar headers lose trailing spaces and tabs. A header or body at EOF gains
a final newline and, with `document-end = "add"`, a `...` marker.
An indentation-only final line loses its spaces when they are not scalar content.
For keep-chomped scalars (`|+` or `>+`), the formatter adds a line break after
removing those spaces to preserve the YAML 1.2 reference parser's value.
When adding a document end marker, it removes only indentation spaces from a final
blank block-scalar line. A root explicit-indent scalar keeps value-bearing spaces;
the marker is left unfixed if appending it would change the reference value.

A document that a tab indents, or that re-indenting would parse differently, is left as
it is and named on stderr.

### Removing an optional document marker

```toml
[format]
document-start = "remove"
```

`---\na: 1\n---\nb: 2\n` becomes `a: 1\n---\nb: 2\n`. Only the first
optional marker is removed. Directives, empty documents and separators keep
required markers. `--- |` becomes `|` on the same line; a marker-line comment
becomes a standalone comment.

## Default profile

With no `[format]` table, `ryl format` writes the profile below. It preserves
existing document start markers, can remove redundant quotes or switch required
double quotes to single, and can indent flush sequences. Migration writes
`quote-style = "preserve"` when `quoted-strings` is disabled in the source preset.

| Default | Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| `quote-style = "single"` | yamlfix's default; see [Quote style](#quote-style) for when it applies |
| `keep-quotes = false` | Removes unnecessary quotes; retaining them is opt-in |
| `line-ending = "lf"` | The default of prettier |
| `document-start = "preserve"` | prettier keeps a file's markers as written |
| `document-end = "preserve"` | No formatter adds `...`; prettier keeps it |
| `prose-wrap = "preserve"` | Prose keeps its line breaks, as under prettier's `proseWrap: "preserve"` |
| `brace-spacing = false` | yamlfix also leaves braces unpadded; prettier pads them |
| `comment-spacing = 2` | The default of ruff and yamlfix |
| `comment-starting-space = "add"` | Adds a space after `#` |
| `max-blank-lines = 2` | Keeps short gaps between content |
| `sequence-style = "preserve"` | Restyling a collection is opt-in |
| `mapping-style = "preserve"` | Restyling a collection is opt-in |
| `sequence-expand = "preserve"` | Rewrapping a flow collection is opt-in |
| `mapping-expand = "preserve"` | Rewrapping a flow collection is opt-in |
| `property-order = "preserve"` | Writers split: prettier and the spec's examples put the tag first, eemeli's `yaml` and libfyaml the anchor |
| `indent-sequences = true` | prettier also indents them |
| `dash-on-own-line = false` | prettier writes `- name: web` |
| `preview = false` | Preview styles are opt-in, as in ruff |
| `line-length = 80` | The default of prettier |
| `indent-width = 2` | The default of prettier and yamlfix |
| Fixed layout above | Every formatter probed agrees |

## Long lines

Use `prose-wrap` for new configs. `fold-long-lines` is legacy; never set both,
even `fold-long-lines = false`.

`prose-wrap` controls paragraphs in plain and quoted values in block context and folded
(`>`) bodies:

- `"preserve"` keeps their physical breaks without joining or wrapping.
- `"always"` joins each paragraph, then wraps it at `line-length` (default 80).
- `"never"` joins each paragraph without wrapping it to the configured width.

!!! note "Wrapping and quotes are separate"

    The default `keep-quotes = false` removes optional quotes, even with
    `prose-wrap = "preserve"`. Set `keep-quotes = true` to keep existing quotes.

```yaml
# before
message: "hello world"

# after, with prose-wrap = "preserve" and keep-quotes = true
message: 'hello world'
```

Paragraph breaks and more-indented folded sections keep their newline semantics.
The prose setting preserves scalar styles, tags, anchors and comments. Literal (`|`)
bodies, keys and flow-context scalars are excluded. Quote normalization remains
independent: retaining optional quoted prose requires [`keep-quotes = true`](#quote-style).

```yaml
# before, or with prose-wrap = "preserve"
message: >
  hello
  world

# after, with prose-wrap = "always" or "never"
message: >
  hello world
```

### Expression wrapping

Under `prose-wrap = "always"`, TOML-only `[[format.prose]]` entries select
scalars by file and mapping path:

```toml
line-length = 60
[format]
prose-wrap = "always"

[[format.prose]]
files = ["*.yaml"]
path = "$.expression"
break-before = ["&&", "||"]
protected-patterns = ['"([^"\\]|\\.)*"', "'([^'\\\\]|\\\\.)*'"]
```

The first entry matching both `files` and `path` wins; entries never merge.
`files` uses [file glob matching](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-ordering/#custom-orders), including
`!` exclusions. `path` uses the same selector subset as custom key ordering:
`$`, `.name`, `['name']`, `[*]` and `.*`. Empty file/token lists, empty or
whitespace-bearing tokens, invalid globs, selectors and regexes are config errors
(exit `2`). `protected-patterns` defaults to an empty list.

Only existing YAML-foldable single spaces before a configured token can break.
The last fitting boundary wins; an overlong clause stays whole. Tabs and double
spaces never become break points. Short expressions join normally; folded
scalars keep their header and chomping mode:

```yaml
expression: >-
  has(object.spec.securityContext)
  && object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true
  && object.spec.securityContext.runAsUser >= 1000
```

Protected regex matches describe the text forms your expressions use, after YAML
quote decoding. Ryl has no embedded-language parser or built-in literal grammar.
Raw/triple quotes, comments and malformed literals need additional patterns or
suppression; ryl cannot prove your patterns cover every literal. Paragraphs,
more-indented content and YAML escapes retain the ordinary prose safety rules.
Other prose policies and `ryl check --fix` ignore the preferences. Without entries,
formatting performs no expression selection, regex matching or decoding.

### Legacy line folding

When `prose-wrap` is absent, `fold-long-lines` defaults to `false`.

With `fold-long-lines = true`, `ryl format` splits scalar lines longer than the top-level
`line-length` (default 80) at single spaces. Folding applies to plain and quoted values
in block context, and folded (`>`) scalar lines at their content indent. For plain and
quoted values, the new line takes the indent of the scalar's existing continuation
lines, or else sits `indent-width` past the column of the collection that owns the value:

```yaml
# before
items:
  - description: This single line is well over eighty characters wide and so the formatter should fold it.
```

```yaml
# after, with fold-long-lines = true
items:
  - description: This single line is well over eighty characters wide and so the
      formatter should fold it.
```

Folded (`>`) scalars keep their content indent; more-indented lines stay whole.
Keys, flow collections, literal (`|`) scalars, and words with no space to break at
stay as they are. Folding ignores the `line-length` rule's own options, and
`ryl check --fix` never folds.

## Collection style

!!! note "Upgrading from 0.28"

    With `sequence-style = "flow"` or `mapping-style = "flow"`, existing long flow
    collections can now become block. Leave the style at `"preserve"` to retain
    existing collection styles, or raise `line-length` to accommodate longer ones.

With `sequence-style` or `mapping-style` set to `"block"`, `ryl format` rewrites flow
collections of that kind in block style, indented by `indent-width`, copying each
entry's text. An inline comment after the collection moves to its key's line:

```yaml
# before
items: [one, two]  # shopping
metadata: {name: example}
```

```yaml
# after, with both set to "block"
items:  # shopping
  - one
  - two
metadata:
  name: example
```

Empty `[]` and `{}` stay flow. A collection that holds a comment, a multi-line entry, a
collection or empty key, or an entry some loaders would read differently in block style
stays as written, and `ryl format` says why on stderr.
So does a collection followed by a ytt `#@` directive on its line, since ytt binds the
directive to the last node on the line, and moving it to the key's line rebinds it.
If the document cannot be re-indented safely, flow collections in that document stay
flow, with a refusal notice. Block-to-flow conversions and conversions in other
documents can still proceed.

When a nested block scalar has only blank body lines before content dedents past its
header, `ryl format` leaves the file unchanged and reports a refusal: the YAML
reference parser can still read the dedented text as scalar content. A sibling key
at the same indent can trigger the same refusal when a sequence dash may move. The same
protection applies when indented `#` text and blank lines form scalar content.
`ryl check --fix` also reports the file, line and reason on stderr and leaves the
file unchanged, apart from independently safe key ordering. In Markdown the refusal
covers only the embedded YAML region that holds the scalar; other regions are still
formatted and fixed.
Compact explicit-key sequences with blank scalar lines are refused when spacing the
header would change the scalar's content indent.
For other block scalars, re-indentation moves value-bearing blank-line spaces with
the scalar header.

With `"flow"`, a block collection of scalars and aliases that is not the document root
becomes one flow line, such as `items: [one, two]`, when it holds no comment and the
line fits `line-length`. Block scalars, multi-line or empty entries, and plain scalars
holding `,[]{}` or starting with `:` or `?` keep it block. A flow collection whose one
line would not fit `line-length` becomes block, and each collection nested in it is
then judged the same way at its new position:

```yaml
# before, with line-length = 30
nested: [[alpha, beta], [delta, epsilon, zeta, eta]]
```

```yaml
# after, with both set to "flow"
nested:
  - [alpha, beta]
  - - delta
    - epsilon
    - zeta
    - eta
```

## Flow line breaks

`sequence-expand` and `mapping-expand` control line breaks inside flow collections:

| Value | Layout |
| :--- | :--- |
| `"preserve"` (default) | Keep existing breaks |
| `"never"` | One line |
| `"always"` | One entry per line |
| `"auto"` | First layout below that fits `line-length` |

`"auto"` tries, in order:

1. One line where the collection starts.
2. One line below its mapping key (for either a sequence or a mapping value).
3. One entry per line.

A spread collection follows
prettier: its opening bracket goes on the line after its key, and every entry ends in a
comma:

```yaml
# before, with line-length = 60
items: [first-item-with-long-name, second-item-with-long-name, third, fourth, fifth]
short: [
  a, b,
  ]
```

```yaml
# after, with sequence-expand = "auto"
items:
  [
    first-item-with-long-name,
    second-item-with-long-name,
    third,
    fourth,
    fifth,
  ]
short: [a, b]
```

At the default `line-length = 80`, the same `items` collection instead fits alone
below the key:

```yaml
# after, with sequence-expand = "auto" and the default line-length
items:
  [first-item-with-long-name, second-item-with-long-name, third, fourth, fifth]
short: [a, b]
```

Flow closing brackets and braces must be deeper than the enclosing block. A closer
at column zero, as below, is repaired and prints
`input was YAML the spec rejects; repaired it`; `--check` exits `1`:

```yaml
# before
items: [
  a, b
]
```

```yaml
# after, with sequence-expand = "preserve"
items: [
  a, b
 ]
```

A trailing comma does not keep a collection spread; with either key set, one before a
bracket on its own line stays, where `ryl format` otherwise removes it. Each nested
collection is judged at
its own line, and one that must spread spreads its parents too. A sequence entry keeps
its `[` on the `-` line, re-indented as the `indentation` rule expects; one after a
second `-` on the line, as in `- - [`, stays as written rather than spread. A comment
after a collection is left out of the width and rules out the move to the next line. A
spread collection keeps its `[` and the comment on the key line, so the comment keeps
its place among the data:

```yaml
# input and output, sequence-expand = "auto"
key: [  # note
  alpha-package-name,
  beta-package-name,
 ]
```

A collection that holds a comment stays as written, with a notice on stderr where its
target rejects its current form. With `*-style = "flow"`, a collection that fits on
one line keeps its `*-expand` layout, and under `"always"` a block collection stays
block rather than become a spread flow one.

## Property order

`property-order` applies to nodes with both an anchor (`&name`) and a tag (`!!seq`).
The default `"preserve"` keeps their order; choose `"anchor-first"` or `"tag-first"`
to normalize it:

```yaml
# before
items: !!seq &list [one, two]

# after, with property-order = "anchor-first"
items: &list !!seq [one, two]
```

## Quote style

By default, `ryl format` quotes a string only where its plain form would load as
something else, using `quote-style`:

```yaml
# before
a: "x"
b: "123"
c: "it's"
d: "tab\there"
e: 'it''s: x'
f: "say \"hi\": x"
```

```yaml
# after, with quote-style = "single"
a: x
b: '123'
c: it's
d: "tab\there"
e: "it's: x"
f: 'say "hi": x'
```

A string that needs quoting takes whichever quotes avoid an escape: single when it
contains `"`, double when it contains only `'`, else `quote-style`. A string that needs
escape sequences stays double-quoted. Physical line breaks alone do not require
double quotes: conversion to single quotes preserves the continuation lines and blank
lines, including their YAML folding. A string that YAML 1.1 loads
as a boolean, such as `"yes"`, `"NO"` or `"on"`, keeps its quotes, so `truthy` stays
clean. So do `"y"`, `"Y"`, `"n"` and `"N"`, which go-yaml v2, and so Kubernetes, loads
as booleans. Mapping keys follow the same rules. A document that declares `%YAML 1.2`,
or any document under the top-level `target-version = "1.2"`, drops those 1.1-only
quotes; see [YAML version compatibility](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/yaml-version/#how-ryl-handles-yaml-versions).

Set `keep-quotes = true` to retain optional quotes while normalizing their character
with the same escape-avoidance rules. Multi-line quoted strings keep their physical
line breaks when their quote character changes. With
`quote-style = "preserve"`, quoting stays untouched regardless of `keep-quotes`.

```toml
[format]
keep-quotes = true
quote-style = "double"
```

```yaml
# before
plain: hello
quoted: 'hello'

# after
plain: hello
quoted: "hello"
```

### Required quotes

When `quoted-strings` is enabled, formatting adds quotes required by `required = true`
or matching `extra-required` patterns. Patterns match decoded values. `check-keys = true`
extends those requirements to keys; ordinary key quote normalization always applies.
`extra-allowed` retains matching existing quotes without adding quotes to plain strings.
Disabled rules retain the formatter's default quoting policy.

```toml
[lint.rules.quoted-strings]
required = false
extra-required = ['\?']
```

```yaml
# before
args: [/health?ready=true]
# after
args: ['/health?ready=true']
```

Only strings under the effective YAML version receive quotes: booleans, numbers,
nulls and YAML 1.1 timestamps stay typed. Explicit version directives override
`target-version`. Wrapped plain strings retain continuation and blank lines under
`prose-wrap = "preserve"`; `"always"` and `"never"` reflow using the selected quoting.
Block scalars stay unchanged.

`quote-style = "preserve"` freezes all quoting, including missing required quotes;
`ryl check` may still report them. `keep-quotes = true` wins over
`required = "only-when-needed"` and warns when retained optional quotes conflict.
`quote-style` and escape avoidance choose the quote character; incompatible lint
`quote-type` or escape exceptions warn with the winning setting and a remedy.

Adding quotes to an implicit key is refused if the selected spelling, including
escapes and properties, would exceed YAML's 1,024-character simple-key limit.
The formatter reports the refusal; shorten the key or use explicit `?` syntax.
Scalars inside an implicit collection key never gain quotes.
Inline suppression and formatter suppression can also leave required quotes missing.
With compatible settings and no collection keys, refusals or suppression, quoted-string output passes
`ryl check` under the same config.

## Preview style

`preview = true` opts in to style changes before they become stable. As in ruff, the
stable style changes only in a minor release, by promoting a preview style, while a
preview style can change in any release. A fix for invalid output, a changed value or a
lost comment can ship in any release. No preview styles exist yet, so `preview` changes
nothing today.

## YAML in Markdown

`ryl format` formats YAML front matter and fenced YAML blocks in Markdown files matched
by `[files].markdown`, as described in [YAML in Markdown](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/markdown/), or every input
given `--markdown`, as with `ryl check`.

If formatting would create a line that closes a YAML fence, ryl leaves that region
unchanged and names the refusal on stderr. Other regions still format. The same guard
applies to editor formatting. When formatting would change a region that mixes CRLF
and LF line endings, ryl leaves the region unchanged with a notice and `--check` /
`--diff` exit `1`. An already formatted mixed region is quiet.

## Suppression

`ryl format` honours the same [inline directives](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/directives/) as `ryl check`: a
`# ryl disable-file` comment leaves the file alone, and
`# ryl disable rule:quoted-strings` or `disable-line rule:quoted-strings` stops
that rule's formatting where it applies. For formatter-only node or region suppression,
use [`format-ignore` or `format-disable` / `format-enable`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/directives/#formatter-only-suppression).
Lint configuration's `[[lint.per-line-ignores]]` and `[lint.per-file-ignores]` suppress
lint findings and safe `check --fix` edits, but do not gate `ryl format`.

## Conflicting lint rules

The formatter's layout is also checked by lint rules, and they stay lint rules:
`ryl check` still reports them, and `ryl check --fix` still fixes the fixable ones. When
one of them is enabled with options that reject what `ryl format` writes, every
`ryl format` run warns on stderr, for example:

```text
warning: the quoted-strings lint rule's options (quote-type = "double", allow-quoted-quotes = false, allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = false) conflict with format.quote-style = "single" and its escape avoidance; format.quote-style wins. Use TOML with lint.rules.quoted-strings.quote-type = "any" and allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = true, or set format.quote-style = "preserve".
```

`--no-warnings` silences it. A rule left at its defaults conflicts only where the table
says so.

| Rule | Conflicts with `ryl format` when |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`braces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/braces/) | `forbid` is set and `[format] mapping-style` is not `"preserve"`, `min-spaces-inside-empty` is above 0, or `min-spaces-inside` to `max-spaces-inside` excludes the `brace-spacing` padding (0, or 1 when `true`) |
| [`brackets`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/brackets/) | `forbid` is set and `[format] sequence-style` is not `"preserve"`, or `min-spaces-inside` or `min-spaces-inside-empty` is above 0 |
| [`commas`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/commas/) | `min-spaces-after` is above 1, or `max-spaces-after` is 0 |
| [`comments`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments/) | `min-spaces-from-content` is above `[format] comment-spacing`, or `max-spaces-from-content` is below it (`-1`, the default, is unlimited); or `ignore-shebangs = false` while `require-starting-space = true` under `[format] comment-starting-space = "add"`, since a shebang keeps its `#!` |
| [`comments-indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/comments-indentation/) | Never |
| [`document-start`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-start/) | `present = false` with `[format] document-start = "add"`, or `present = true` with `"remove"` |
| [`document-end`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/document-end/) | `present = false` with `[format] document-end = "add"` |
| [`empty-lines`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-lines/) | `max` is below `[format] max-blank-lines` |
| [`new-line-at-end-of-file`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-line-at-end-of-file/) | Never |
| [`new-lines`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/new-lines/) | `type` resolves to a different ending from `[format] line-ending`, or `line-ending = "auto"`, which writes either |
| [`quoted-strings`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/quoted-strings/) | See below; never under `quote-style = "preserve"` |
| [`trailing-spaces`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/trailing-spaces/) | Never |
| [`colons`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/colons/) | `max-spaces-after` is 0 |
| [`hyphens`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/hyphens/) | `max-spaces-after` is 0, or `dash-on-own-line = true` while `[format] dash-on-own-line = false` |
| [`indentation`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/indentation/) | `spaces` is a number other than `indent-width` (2 when unset); or `indent-sequences` is the opposite of `[format] indent-sequences` |
| [`line-length`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/line-length/) | Never; folding is opt-in and leaves lines it cannot break |

The table compares formatter settings with lint options; it does not promise every
finding can be fixed. A keep-chomped (`|+`/`>+`) tail can exceed `empty-lines max`, and
trailing spaces inside a block scalar can remain findings after `ryl format` and
`ryl check --fix` because removing them would change the scalar value.

`quoted-strings` accepts the formatter's output for every supported `required` mode
and `extra-required` pattern when `quote-type` is either `"any"` or matches
`quote-style`. A `quote-type` of `"single"` or `"double"` also needs
`allow-quoted-quotes = true`, for strings quoted to avoid an escape. Under
`required = "only-when-needed"`, set `allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = true`
to retain optional escaped double quotes, including a literal backslash.
A single-quote lint preference also needs the escape exception for necessary escapes.
The rule's defaults (`required = true`) add quotes:

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[lint.rules]
quoted-strings = "enable"
```

These quoted-strings configs accept the formatter's output:

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[lint.rules.quoted-strings]
quote-type = "any"
required = "only-when-needed"
allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = true
```

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[lint.rules.quoted-strings]
quote-type = "single"
required = "only-when-needed"
allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = true
allow-quoted-quotes = true
```

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[format]
quote-style = "double"

[lint.rules.quoted-strings]
quote-type = "double"
required = "only-when-needed"
allow-double-quotes-for-escaping = true
allow-quoted-quotes = true
```

A YAML config cannot set `allow-double-quotes-for-escaping`. To accept optional
escaped quotes there, use `quote-type: any` and `required: false`:

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```yaml
rules:
  quoted-strings:
    quote-type: any
    required: false
```

The other conflicts follow the table:

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-conflict -->
```toml
[format]
document-start = "add"

[lint.rules.document-start]
present = false
```

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[lint.rules.document-start]
present = false
```

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[format]
brace-spacing = true

[lint.rules.braces]
min-spaces-inside = 1
max-spaces-inside = 1
min-spaces-inside-empty = 0
max-spaces-inside-empty = 0
```

<!-- ryl-config-check: format-clean -->
```toml
[lint.rules.commas]
max-spaces-after = -1

[lint.rules.comments]
max-spaces-from-content = -1
```

The other eleven rules check things `ryl format` never changes, so they never conflict
with it: [`anchors`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/anchors/),
[`block-scalar-chomping`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/block-scalar-chomping/),
[`empty-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/empty-values/), [`float-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/float-values/),
[`key-duplicates`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-duplicates/), [`key-ordering`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/key-ordering/),
[`merge-keys`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/merge-keys/), [`octal-values`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/octal-values/),
[`tags`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/tags/), [`truthy`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/truthy/) and
[`unicode-line-breaks`](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/unicode-line-breaks/). `truthy` and `key-ordering` keep
their `ryl check --fix` fixes.

## Recommended lint config

To lint alongside `ryl format`, start from the
[recommended starter config](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/quickstart/#lint-alongside-ryl-format),
which enables only rules the formatter never touches and leaves layout to
`ryl format --check`.

## Running with `ryl check --fix`

`# ryl format-ignore` and formatter regions do not stop `ryl check --fix` from
rewriting protected nodes; lint fixes remain active.

Run `ryl check --fix` before `ryl format`, in a pre-commit or prek config as on the
command line, so the formatter has the last word on layout; ruff gives the same order
for `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format`. Re-indenting can still push a line past
`line-length`, which the `line-length` rule then reports (see
[Conflicting lint rules](#conflicting-lint-rules)), so lint a formatted file rather than
relying on the check that ran before formatting.

## Exit codes

| Code | `ryl format` | `ryl format --check` / `--diff` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Files formatted, or nothing to do | No file would change; a symlinked input is refused on stderr but still exits `0` |
| `1` | Not used | At least one file would change, a mixed-newline Markdown region needs formatting, or a ragged Markdown region retains layout findings |
